subject: HelixPay go-live: tactical ask for model affinity and warm-cache window
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HelixPay go-live: tactical ask for model affinity and warm-cache window

Marissa / Karthik —

Quick background: HelixPay is targeting a limited go-live on 2027-05-02 for an embedded payments assistant. They want hard SLOs for 99th pct latency and are asking for a short-term guarantee we can provide during their ramp (first 72 hours).

As we discussed on the call, the clearest path to reduce tail latency and throttling risk is a temporary model affinity policy + a warm-cache window (pre-warm KV/prefix cache across their tenant) for the 48–72 hours around the launch. They are willing to take a short-term billback for warm cache if we can pin capacity and ensure affinity to avoid noisy neighbors.

Ask: can Product/Eng approve an exception to the model affinity rule for a single enterprise tenant (HelixPay) and surface a tactical warm-cache plan we can run as an EAP? Specifically:
- Confirm feasibility of tenant-level affinity (pin to a small dedicated pool) and any expected timeline to enable for an EAP (hours/days).
- Rough cost estimate for a 72-hour warm-cache + reserved burst (ballpark $).
- Any risks to general serving (cache eviction, billing complexity) and suggested mitigations.

I attached the Helix go-live MAMP and launch playbook draft. If we can get a short internal decision this week I can lock the doc with Helix and get their procurement moving.

Attachments: Helix_MAMP_MAP.pdf (launch checklist, traffic profile)

Thanks —
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixPay go-live: tactical ask for model affinity and warm-cache window

Dylan —

Thanks for the context and for flagging the timeline. High level: Product is open to short-lived exceptions for strategic deals but we need concrete guardrails to avoid precedence creep. Before we green-light anything I need:

1) Expected RPS and peak concurrency during the 72-hour window (Helix estimate).
2) A clear rollback policy and a documented canary plan (metrics to watch + thresholds to trigger rollback).
3) A cost-recovery proposal (how much of the warm-cache/burst we bill vs absorb).

If we proceed we'll require Eng to provide an implementation note with: affinity scope, how polytenant routing will be bypassed, and a timeline for enabling/disabling. Also cc'ing Mina for any QA/eval constraints around correctness and model drift during a pinned run.

I attached a short tech-impact template you can fill with Helix numbers — helps us speed review.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. PM, Product — Redwood Inference

Attachment: tech-impact-summary.pdf

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixPay go-live: tactical ask for model affinity and warm-cache window

Folks —

Feasibility notes from Eng:
- Tenant-level affinity: technically straightforward as a short-lived policy. We can route HelixPay to a small reserved pool and mark their requests with a tenancy tag. Implementation effort: ~1–2 engineer-days to add the bypass flag to routing + one small infra change to reserve the pool.
- Warm-cache: we can seed KV/prefix cache and run a scheduled re-seed for the 72-hour window. Cost: rough estimate attached (see estimate_warm_cache_costs.xlsx). Expect an incremental infra cost and increased token-serving cost due to pre-warm generation.
- Risk: affinity reduces packing efficiency; if Helix has unexpectedly high traffic it could starve other tenants unless we reserve slices/burst bucket. We recommend reserving a small dedicated pool (N GPUs) for the window and enabling automatic fallback to their tiered fallback after threshold X requests.

Operational asks for Sales/CS to confirm asap:
1) Helix's 95th/99th latency SLAs required and their acceptable burst budget.
2) Whether Helix will accept a billback model for the warm-cache (they indicated yes on the call, but need written confirmation).
3) Who owns on-call for the 72-hour window on the customer side (we need a named contact).

If we get the above I can carve out a reserve and schedule the infra changes. CC'ing Mina for QA items (evaluation baselines to monitor model behavior while pinned).

Attachment: estimate_warm_cache_costs.xlsx

Team / Helix —

Thanks everyone for the quick turn. Summary and proposed mutual action plan (MAP):

- Product: Marissa, thanks for the go/no-go criteria. We will populate the tech-impact template with Helix's numbers by EOD today.
- Eng: Karthik, thanks for the feasibility note and cost estimate. Action: carve a 3-GPU reserve for 72 hours and enable a tenancy affinity flag starting 12:00 UTC on 2027-05-02. Eng to provide a one-page runbook by 2027-04-20.
- CS/Sales: Grace and I will get written confirmation from Helix on billback and the named on-call contact this afternoon.

Helix (Katie / Raj): can you confirm these three items to proceed?
1) Final expected peak concurrency and RPS during go-live window (numbers for the tech-impact template).
2) Agreement to a billback covering warm-cache generation and reserve compute for the 72-hour window (we will share the cost estimate).
3) A single on-call engineer name + phone for the window.

If Helix confirms, we'll move to Docs: I will share a DocuSign for the short-term activation addendum and post the HubSpot note (link below). Please reply with confirmations or any redlines.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/helixpay | DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/contract/HELX-2027-01-signature | Jira: INF-4821
